creative_context.references: Led Zeppelin, classic rock guitar riffs

generation_attempts.input_content: Electric guitar riff, classic rock, E minor, distorted tone, powerful
generation_attempts.output_description: Interesting riff but audio quality is very poor - lots of spectrogram artifacts, muddy frequency response. Riff idea is decent though.
generation_attempts.notable_observations: Riffusion has inherent audio quality limitations due to spectrogram approach. Musical idea is there but fidelity is low.

generation_attempts.input_content: Heavy electric guitar power riff, distortion, palm muted, driving rhythm
generation_attempts.output_description: Better! Palm muting is recognized. Riff has good energy. Still has frequency artifacts in high end (cymbals/noise bleeding in).
generation_attempts.notable_observations: Lower denoising helped reduce muddiness. 'Palm muted' keyword effective for tight rhythmic riffs.

generation_attempts.input_content: Distorted electric guitar riff, bluesy rock, E minor pentatonic, gritty tone, isolated guitar
generation_attempts.output_description: Best result - bluesy feel captured well, E minor pentatonic scale recognized. Added 'isolated guitar' helped reduce extra instruments. Still has artifacts but manageable with EQ.
generation_attempts.notable_observations: Specifying 'isolated guitar' reduces multi-instrument bleeding. 'Bluesy', 'gritty', 'pentatonic' keywords all effective.

prompt_refinement.initial: Electric guitar riff, classic rock, E minor, distorted tone, powerful
prompt_refinement.final: Distorted electric guitar riff, bluesy rock, E minor pentatonic, gritty tone, isolated guitar
prompt_refinement.iterations: Three attempts: (1) Basic prompt, poor quality, (2) Added technique (palm muted), (3) Added isolation + scale + style adjectives
prompt_refinement.responds_well: Playing techniques (palm muted), scale names (pentatonic), style descriptors (bluesy, gritty), 'isolated guitar' for reducing bleed
prompt_refinement.struggles_with: Audio fidelity (inherent to spectrogram approach), preventing multi-instrument bleed entirely
prompt_refinement.unexpected: 'Isolated guitar' keyword helps but doesn't eliminate bleed completely
prompt_refinement.effective_keywords: bluesy, gritty, palm muted, pentatonic, isolated, distorted, driving

separation.quality: Tried but guitar already isolated enough

eq.details: Aggressive high-shelf cut above 8kHz to remove spectral artifacts. Boost at 1.5-2kHz for presence.

compression.details: Heavy compression to even out dynamics and add sustain

reverb.details: Short room reverb to add space and mask some artifacts

post_processing.other: Added subtle saturation to enhance grit and mask digital artifacts

daw_integration.context: Used as main guitar riff for rock track, layered with live bass and drums
daw_integration.workarounds: Manual tempo warping needed - Riffusion doesn't respect BPM spec. Set warp markers at downbeats.

reflections.what_worked: Riffusion is fast and captures musical ideas quickly. Good for ideation/sketching. Playing technique keywords (palm muted) and style descriptors (bluesy, gritty) are effective.
reflections.frustrations: Audio quality is significantly worse than MusicGen or DDSP. Inherent spectrogram artifacts require heavy post-processing. Multi-instrument bleed is hard to eliminate. BPM/key control is approximate at best.
reflections.discoveries: 'Isolated guitar' keyword helps reduce multi-instrument bleed (not perfect but noticeable). Heavy EQ and reverb can mask artifacts enough for background use.
reflections.comparisons: Fastest generation time (7-8s) but worst audio quality. Trade-off between speed and fidelity. Better for quick ideation than final production. MusicGen has better quality, DDSP has better control.
reflections.emotional_state: Frustrated by quality limitations but appreciated the speed for rapid iteration. Acceptable for sketching but wouldn't use for foreground elements.
